_comment: Written by admin/build/compare_tests.py. Each entry is one executed check against the live service using a published read key. Re-run the script to refresh.

tests.claim: A published read key alone opens the vault and lists its files
tests.evidence: 4 files listed from vault 4bshby5n; HEAD obj-cas-imm-abfb17bf6c21
tests.fails_if: the ref cannot be derived, fetched or decrypted with the read key alone

tests.claim: The bytes the server returns are unreadable without the key
tests.evidence: 489 raw bytes: not valid UTF-8; the same object decrypts to 461 bytes of JSON with the read key
tests.fails_if: the raw response decodes as text without decryption

tests.claim: Objects are content-addressed and byte-identical on re-fetch
tests.evidence: two fetches of obj-cas-imm-abfb17bf6c21 returned identical bytes (sha256 abfb17bf6c21472d…) — which is why a copy already taken stays readable
tests.fails_if: the same object id returns different bytes

tests.claim: A vault app can be granted write over one folder and nothing else
tests.fails_if: the declaration is missing or grants write beyond adherence/

tests.claim: A read-only clone cannot commit or push
tests.evidence: commit exit 1, push exit 1; no vault_key on disk; "error: This vault was cloned read-only. To write, re-clone with the fu"
tests.fails_if: commit or push succeeds, or a write credential is present on disk

tests.claim: The CLI accepts the canonical sgit_rk1_ prefix the web loader accepts
tests.evidence: sgit-ai v0.14.27: prefixed clone failed — derived ref afdb9d843131 instead of 11ea50e81f4d; the bare <64hex>:<vault_id> form works on the same version
tests.fails_if: the prefixed form derives a ref id different from the bare form
